svg.title: A lead II ECG with the corresponding arterial blood pressure
svg.desc: Top: arterial blood pressure in mm Hg versus time t over two heartbeats of 0.75 s each, swinging between a diastolic minimum of about 83 mm Hg and a systolic maximum of about 125 mm Hg, with a small dicrotic notch after each peak. Bottom: the lead II ECG voltage in millivolts over the same time. Each beat shows a small P wave, the sharp QRS complex peaking at about 1.0 mV at R, and a broad T wave. The systolic peak in pressure follows shortly after the QRS complex, which is caused by the depolarization and contraction of the ventricles.
